deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a scheme over a base S. P^n (written P^{n*} on the previous page) is the ring of principal parts of X^{n+1}/S along the diagonal: either infinitesimal neighbourhoods of some order or the formal completion. Read as a pro-object, P^* is a cosimplicial ring. It is the coordinate ring of the formal (infinitesimal) groupoid of X/S, and its cofaces and codegeneracies come from projections and diagonals of the X^{n+1}.

What the page does.
1. Grothendieck sets Q^i = P^{i+1}, the décalage (shift) of the cosimplicial ring P^*. On Q^i, O_X acts through the extra factor, i.e. the 'external right' structure, and this action commutes with the shifted cosimplicial structure.
2. Given an O_X-Module M, he forms Q^i[M] = Q^i ⊗_{O_X} M, the tensor taken over that external right structure. Read as pro-objects or completed, these form a cosimplicial object Q^*[M]. It is in fact a cosimplicial Module over the cosimplicial ring P^*, through the remaining factors. It is functorial in M ∈ Mod(X/S).
3. The 'highly special' property is that the Q^i[M] are obtained from one another by base change along the structure maps P^i → P^j. In modern terms, Q^*[M] is a cartesian (cocartesian) cosimplicial module over P^*, i.e. an object of the 2-limit (the 'lim' with underlined arrow) of the categories of P^i-Modules. A cartesian cosimplicial module over the infinitesimal groupoid is exactly a stratified module, i.e. a crystal on the infinitesimal site.

The next page draws the conclusion. Q^0[M] = P^1 ⊗ M = P(M), the (pro-)Module of principal parts of M, carries a canonical stratification relative to S. M is recovered from it via a subsheaf of special sections.

This is the 'linearization' functor L(M) = P_X ⊗ M, which turns modules and differential operators into crystals and linear maps. It is the ingredient for comparing crystalline/infinitesimal cohomology with de Rham cohomology, via the linearized de Rham complex and a Poincaré-lemma argument.

The shift construction has an extra codegeneracy. That makes the augmented object Q^* contractible onto O_X, which is the conceptual reason the linearized complex resolves M.
errors: No mathematical error. Grothendieck himself flags the one gap: the tensor products must be read as pro-objects or completed. Only under finiteness hypotheses (noetherian X, M of finite type) can they be treated as genuine sheaves; the previous and next pages say this explicitly.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial ring P^* of principal parts (formal groupoid of X/S) and its décalage Q^i = P^{i+1}, with O_X acting through the extra factor
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander / infinitesimal groupoid cosimplicial ring and its décalage (path object)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals, 1966-68); Berthelot (1974); Illusie for systematic use of décalage
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés (1968), discusses stratifications via P^n; the explicit cosimplicial décalage formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Q^*[M] = Q^* ⊗ M as a cosimplicial P^*-Module, functorial in M
ideas.modern_name: Linearization L(M) of a module / differential operators
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés 'Crystals' (linearization ideas); fully in Berthelot's thesis

ideas.what: Cartesian (base-change-compatible) cosimplicial modules over P^* are equivalent to stratified modules (crystals)
ideas.modern_name: Crystals as cartesian cosimplicial modules / descent along the infinitesimal groupoid
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968); descent formalism in SGA1 VI/VIII

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, early cosimplicial formulation of linearization: principal parts as a cartesian cosimplicial module over the shifted groupoid ring. The content matches what is in Grothendieck's 1966-68 crystals lectures and was later systematized by Berthelot and Berthelot–Ogus. It is historically nice as a draft of the 'laïus' but not new.
transcription_corrections: The bracket under the tensor sign reads '[str. ext. dr.]' (structure extérieure droite), not '[str. dr.]'. It specifies that ⊗_{O_X} uses the external right O_X-structure.
First line: 'Q^i = P^{i+1}' is confirmed by the image ('Q^i = P^{i+1}' written with superscript i+1).
The struck word before 'cosimplicial' is a false start ('co-' / 'en-co'), so the phrase reads 'un objet cosimplicial'.
Final line: 'objets d'une lim' with an underlined left-pointing arrow under 'lim', i.e. a projective/2-limit of categories, consistent with cartesian sections.
